title: Green Eggs and Ham's 50-word bet
hook: One of the best-selling children's books was written to win a 50-dollar bet.
peek: Dr. Seuss's publisher bet him 50 dollars that he could not write a whole book using only 50 different words. Seuss won, and the result was Green Eggs and Ham, published in 1960 and still selling in huge numbers.
lede: Bennett Cerf, co-founder of Random House, knew Dr. Seuss had just written The Cat in the Hat with a small vocabulary. So he bet him 50 dollars that he could not write a book with just 50 different words. Seuss, whose real name was Theodor Geisel, took the bet. Green Eggs and Ham came out in 1960, with exactly 50.

bullets.text: The earlier challenge came from an educational publisher who wanted a lively reader to replace dull school primers. Seuss had to work from a list of simple words, and The Cat in the Hat, in 1957, used 236 of them.

Of the 50 words in Green Eggs and Ham, all but one have a single syllable. The exception is "anywhere". Repetition does the rest, as Sam-I-Am offers the dish in a box, with a fox, on a train and in the rain.
The story usually told is that Cerf never actually handed over the 50 dollars. Seuss came out well ahead anyway, since the book became one of the best-selling children's books in English.
